newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Spending would ease monetary pressure - NZ Labour.
newsitem.headline: Spending would ease monetary pressure - NZ Labour.

text.p: New Zealand Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen said on Wednesday the party's spending plans would help to ease pressure on monetary policy.
Cullen said there was currently "excessive" pressure on monetary policy despite surpluses being run by the conservative National Party government.
"Already we see, despite large surpluses, excessive pressure on monetary policy, and some of our spending will in fact ease that," he told Radio New Zealand.

"If we're putting money into training, that eases the labour market. If we're putting money into housing, that eases the housing market. Reducing student fees, that has a direct impact of course on the CPI."
Cullen said that Labour, while raising government spending, would still be repaying public debt and running "the strongest fiscal position of any developed country".

Labour, currently the main opposition party, is running about neck-and-neck with the economic nationalist New Zealand First Party for second place behind the government in opinion polls leading up to a general election on October 12.
The polls suggest a possible change of government if Labour, NZ First and the left-wing Alliance can reach agreement.
